unverified: The widely repeated claim that PayPal was losing 'over $10 million a month' to fraud in 2000, against 'under $1 million a month' of revenue. PayPal's own audited filing discloses $11.0 million of provision for transaction losses for the whole of 2000 and $14.5 million of revenue for the year. The monthly figure traces to Levchin's later retellings (Livingston, Founders at Work, 2007; Jackson, The PayPal Wars, 2004), neither of which I could open in full. Not used in the prose; the filed nine-month figures are used instead.
That Igor was named after a specific fraudster who taunted PayPal by name. The contemporaneous source says only 'after a Russian hacker it helped detect'.
The $1.5 billion price eBay paid for PayPal in 2002. The Palantir S-1 confirms the acquisition and its year, not the amount, and I did not open the merger agreement. Not used.
Joe Lonsdale and Nathan Gettings as Palantir co-founders. The S-1 defines its 'Founders' as Alexander Karp, Stephen Cohen and Peter Thiel only. Not used.

Any claim that Palantir's decomposition interview round is described in a Palantir source, or that Palantir consciously modelled it on the PayPal fraud desk. The causal chain in the story runs hazard -> job -> exam and stops at the job; the exam is the chapter's own reporting from candidates.
Whether Levchin's team ever attempted, and abandoned, a fully unattended version of Igor. No source I opened says so.
